AfterCardPlayed.issue: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13): STALE -- AND THE RECORD'S PREMISE WAS BACKWARDS. The old text read that C# skips Hook.AfterCardPlayed entirely when the play ended the combat (claiming CardModel.cs:1957 gates on CombatManager.IsInProgress) while the sim always fires it. That is a misreading: Hook.cs:275-276's own comment says this hook deliberately BYPASSES IterateCombatHookListeners precisely so it 'completes resolution of the card that caused the kill', and IsInProgress is still true on the lethal iteration (it is cleared from CheckWinCondition, which runs after the whole play action -- ActionExecutor.cs:161-171). C# DOES dispatch on the killing iteration. The sim's current `if not self.is_over:` gate gets this right: it does not suppress the killing iteration but does suppress genuinely-later dispatches against an already-over combat. Pinned by test/test_r13_relic1.py::test_pen_nib_tenth_attack_that_ends_combat_still_unmarks.  The text it replaced read: Rollup of guards G1 and G3. Executed: a Throwing-Axe-replayed 10th Strike costs the enemy 24 HP in the sim (12 + 12) against the game's 18 (12 + 6) -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-pennib.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE at the sim's own preview site): the entire `AttackToDouble == null` arm of ModifyDamageMultiplicative (PenNib.cs:120-128) has no counterpart -- the game doubles the PENDING 10th Attack's number for any cardSource that is not in PileType.Play once AttacksPlayed == 9
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The preview arm is ported. PenNib.cs:120-128's `if (AttackToDouble == null) { CardPile? pile = cardSource.Pile; if ((pile == null || pile.Type != PileType.Play) && AttacksPlayed == 9) return 2m; }` now exists in relics/pen_nib.py, with the pile clause intact and the two preceding C# guards it also lacked (`cardSource == null` at :112 and the dealer test at :116) written out beside it. The sim's PileType.Play analogue is `player._playing_card`, which `_resolve_card_play` sets for the duration of the play -- so the arm can only be taken for a card that is NOT being played, which is what stops the real tenth Attack doubling twice. EXECUTED: with `_attacks_played = 9` and a Strike in hand, `previews.preview_card_damage` now returns 12 where it returned 6 and the game prints 12; at `_attacks_played = 3` it still returns 6; and actually PLAYING the tenth Attack still deals 12, not 24. Filed and fixed as a gap rather than waived under the presentation exclusion because the sim's consumer of this number is the policy's observation vector (full_env builds it per (card, enemy) pair), not a sprite.  Pinned by test/test_relic_live_tail.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: PenNib.cs:120-128 reads `CardPile? pile = cardSource.Pile; if ((pile == null || pile.Type != PileType.Play) && AttacksPlayed == 9) return 2m;`. A card mid-OnPlay is in PileType.Play (PROMPT.md bug class 7), so this arm can only be taken for a card that is NOT being played -- i.e. a card in hand whose damage the game is PREVIEWING. It is the relic's promise made visible: with nine Attacks played, the tenth shows its doubled face before you commit. pen_nib.py:44 keys solely on `card is self._card_to_double`, which before_card_played sets only during the play, so the sim's preview never doubles. REACHABILITY (LIVE and executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-pennib): the sim HAS the preview path and consumes it as an RL feature, not only as UI -- previews.preview_card_damage (previews.py:149-158) replays the same modifier chain as DamageCmd.deal and full_env.py:510 calls it per (card, enemy) pair to build the observation. Observed with _attacks_played = 9 and a Strike in hand: preview_card_damage = 6 where the game prints 12; the damage actually DEALT is 12 on both sides, so the divergence is confined to the previewed/observed number. Filed as a gap rather than waived under the presentation exclusion for exactly that reason: the sim's consumer of this number is the policy's observation vector, not a sprite. The fix must keep the pile clause or the real play would double twice. NOTE per binding rule 7: previews.py, full_env.py and cmds.py are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G3 (DORMANT): C# skips Hook.AfterCardPlayed entirely when the play ended the combat (CardModel.cs:1957 gates on CombatManager.IsInProgress) while combat.py:514 always fires it, so a game-side 10th Attack that lands the killing blow stays MARKED and the sim's does not
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the mark (AttackToDouble / _card_to_double) is cleared only by the AfterCardPlayed handler. C#'s dispatch of that hook is conditional, the sim's is not, so the two codebases can leave the relic in different states after a combat-ending Attack -- and because a C# deck CardModel is the same instance combat after combat, a stale mark would double that exact card for free in the NEXT fight. DORMANT and named as such: this is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json guard G8's mechanism (Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners yields nothing once CombatManager.IsOverOrEnding is true; the sim has no gate at all), which that record labels DORMANT and pins as a strict xfail at test/test_hook_order.py::TestTurnStructureOrder (test_hook_order.py:1178 test_no_listener_runs_after_the_combat_starts_ending). One verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3, so this entry matches rather than re-derives. Stated plainly as a limit of this audit: I did NOT establish by execution that C#'s IsInProgress is already false at the instant that dispatch is reached, so the killing-blow consequence is an unconfirmed corollary of a mechanism another record owns. The concrete thing that would make it live is a fix to the sim's dispatch gate without a matching reset of _card_to_double. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardModel.cs, combat.py, test_hook_order.py and hook_dispatch.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: `_attacks_played` and `_card_to_double` are never reset at a combat boundary in the sim -- and AttacksPlayed is never reset at one in the game either. The sweep row `pen_nib  C# resets: NONE (may be per-run by design)` is CORRECT here
guards.rationale: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` flags both fields and .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md lists pen_nib among five relics deserving a second look. Settled: AttacksPlayed is a [SavedProperty] (PenNib.cs:53-66) so it survives a save/load, PenNib.cs overrides no combat-boundary hook at all, and its only mutator is the setter -- so 'every 10th Attack you play' is a run-level count on both sides. The sim's relic instance lives on RunState.relics and is re-attached to every CombatState (run.py:1153), which is precisely the persistence this needs. Same family and same verdict as relic/happy_flower N1 and relic/fake_happy_flower N1 (binding rule 3). PROMPT.md bug class 13 wants the reader-trace before clearing a missing reset: the readers are before_card_played and modify_damage_multiplicative, and a run-level counter is what both are supposed to see. `_card_to_double`'s cross-combat behaviour is guard G3's subject, not this entry's. NOTE per binding rule 7: this rationale leans on relic_probes.py, content-relic-sweeps.md, run.py, happy_flower.json and fake_happy_flower.json, none of which this record hashes.

guards.what: N2: `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` on BeforeCardPlayed (PenNib.cs:142-145) and `dealer != base.Owner.Osty` on the multiplicative (PenNib.cs:116)
guards.rationale: Two separate out-of-scope clauses. The card-owner check is multiplayer scoping: the sim has one player and CombatState dispatches card hooks only for that player's plays, so it is structurally satisfied. Osty is the NECROBINDER's pet -- Player.Osty is `PlayerCombatState?.GetPet<Osty>()` (src/Core/Entities/Players/Player.cs:132) and its model is src/Core/Models/Monsters/Osty.cs, referenced from Necrobinder cards and from Achievements/SkillNecrobinder2Achievement.cs. The sim is Ironclad-only and has no pet creature, so `dealer is self.player` (pen_nib.py:44) is the complete single-character form of C#'s two-way test. Waived under the shared contract's multiplayer and other-characters exclusions, not under an unreachability claim about ported content. NOTE per binding rule 7: Player.cs, Osty.cs and SkillNecrobinder2Achievement.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: `if (!props.IsPoweredAttack()) return 1m;` (PenNib.cs:108-111) -- the sim's modify_damage_multiplicative takes no props argument at all
guards.rationale: Structurally satisfied at BOTH sim call sites rather than dropped: cmds.py:56 wraps the additive+multiplicative stage in `if is_powered_attack(props):` and previews.py:55 repeats the identical gate, and valueprops.is_powered_attack (valueprops.py:47-49) is a line-for-line port of ValuePropExtensions.IsPoweredAttack (src/Core/ValueProps/ValuePropExtensions.cs:5-12, `Move && !Unpowered`). So an unpowered or non-Move damage packet never reaches the relic's method in the sim, which is what the C# early return achieves. Checked deliberately because omitting the parameter makes the guard invisible in the relic file. The one sim caller that bypasses the gate is cards/thrash.py:47, which calls modify_damage_multiplicative directly with a Creature in the `card` slot, so pen_nib's `card is self._card_to_double` test cannot match and the relic returns 1.0 there regardless. NOTE per binding rule 7: cmds.py, previews.py, valueprops.py, cards/thrash.py and ValuePropExtensions.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N4: `_attacksThreshold = 10` (PenNib.cs:15) is declared and never read -- every arithmetic site uses a bare literal (PenNib.cs:33, :63, and `== 9` at :123)
guards.rationale: ATTACKS = 10 (pen_nib.py:23) is the sim's single constant and it feeds the only arithmetic the port performs (`(self._attacks_played + 1) % self.ATTACKS`, pen_nib.py:33). No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension appears anywhere in the file, so 10 is the pinned non-ascension value, and the `AttacksPlayed == 9` form of the same threshold (which the missing preview arm needs, guard G2) is ATTACKS - 1. Recorded because PROMPT.md bug class 19 is a wrong constant hiding behind a citation that looks verified: here the unused const, the three literals and the sim constant all agree at 10.

guards.what: N5: C# marks the card only when the counter WRAPS (`if (AttacksPlayed == 0) AttackToDouble = cardPlay.Card;`, PenNib.cs:147-150) -- the mark is set for the attack that IS the tenth, not the one after it
guards.rationale: pen_nib.py:34-35 is the same test against the same post-increment value, and both sides take the modulo inside the increment so 'wrapped to 0' means 'this was the 10th'. Worth an entry because the off-by-one is easy to get backwards and it is the hinge of guard G2's `AttacksPlayed == 9` preview test: after nine attacks the counter reads 9 and the NEXT play is the doubled one. Executed as a by-product of b12-pennib, where priming _attacks_played = 9 makes the very next Strike deal 12 instead of 6.
